title: An if/else Statement in MIPS Assembly
description: Use beq and an unconditional jump j to branch between two outcomes when comparing a user guess against a secret number.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: In `main`, print the prompt string `input` with syscall 4, read an integer from the user into `$v0` with syscall 5, and load the secret number `7` into `$s0`.
`beq $s0, $v0, correct` compares `$s0` and `$v0` and branches to `correct` if they are equal. Otherwise execution continues to lines 21-23 to print `wrong` and then jumps to `exit` on line 26.
The `correct:` label prints the string `right`, `exit:` terminates the program with syscall 10, and `.data` defines the three null-terminated `.asciiz` strings.
Look at how the two branches are laid out: when `beq` does not branch, the fall-through block prints `wrong` and uses `j exit` to jump past the `correct:` label.

steps.question: If the integer in `$v0` after syscall 5 is not 7, which instruction executes immediately after `beq $s0, $v0, correct` on line 18?
steps.answer: Line 21 (`li $v0, 4`), which begins the syscall sequence to print the `wrong` string `"Not quite!\n"`.

steps.description: At line 18, `beq` compares `$s0` (7) with `$v0`; since they are not equal in this run, the branch is not taken.
Line 23 executes syscall 4 to print `Not quite!`, and line 26 then jumps to `exit`.
